title: Burn velocity & pricing sensitivity workbook
content:
Objective:
This workbook synthesizes an 18-month headcount plan with three tiered pricing sensitivity scenarios to show impact on gross burn, net runway, and required token-price adjustments to keep margin targets. Intended as a working sheet for Q1 planning + headcount gating decisions. Draft — inputs are rough, flagged where we need validation from Recruiting/Eng leads.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Base hiring plan (plan A) adds 28 FTEs over 12 months (eng heavy: serving/runtime + infra + observability). Peak monthly burn with hiring/phased ramp: ~$5.9M.
- Scenario outcomes:
  • Baseline pricing (current list): runway = ~14.7 months on committed cash ($80M) with current consumption growth assumptions.
  • Price-down (-10% unit price to win GTM deals): runway shortens to ~12.3 months unless offset by 22% uplift in consumption volume (unlikely short-term).
  • Price-up (+12% premium / enterprise packaging): extends runway to ~17.2 months if churn stays <2% and adoption of dedicated/private increases 5 p.p.
- Key ask: hold on non-critical hiring in Q1 unless we can commit a 6–8% price uplift for enterprise feature bundles (security + retention).

Sheet layout & key tabs (notes):
- Inputs: baseline revenue by product (hosted API / dedicated / private), average unit price per 1k tokens, active customers, ARR by cohort, gross margin assumptions, fixed opex, SaaS sales ramp assumptions.
- HC_plan: hires by role/team, onboarding ramp months, fully-burdened cost (salary + benefits + infra chargeback) per hire.
- Burn_model: month-by-month P&L-ish cash flow (non-GAAP) for 18 months with scenario toggles.
- Pricing_sensitivity: table that sweeps price delta (-15%..+20%) vs volume delta (-30%..+50%) and produces runway map and break-even price for each hiring posture.
- Risk_log: qualitative mitigants and dependencies (recruiting lead time, capacity/GPUs commitments, sales cycle length).
- Action_items: owners + dates.

Selected assumptions (inputs to validate with teams):
- Starting cash: $80,000,000 (post-Series C run-rate).
- Fixed opex (G&A + office comps + support): $650k/mo base. Escalation: 3% qtrly comp inflation baked into hiring costs.
- Revenue mix (starting month): Hosted API 58% of revenue, Dedicated 26%, Private 16%.
- Average price per 1k tokens (hosted): $0.018 (base). Embedding pricing and dedicated/unitized rates included in tab.
- Consumption growth (baseline): +6% MoM net usage by product; conservative: +2% MoM; aggressive: +10% MoM.
- Gross margin (post infra): Hosted 55%, Dedicated 48%, Private 42% (includes customer-managed infra discounts).
- Hiring cadence (Plan A): 28 FTEs = 16 Eng (serving/runtime 7, infra 4, sre/observability 3, devexp 2), 6 Product/Design, 4 Sales/CS/BD, 2 Finance/People ops. Hiring starts Jan 2026 with staged onboard ramp (50% productivity first 2 months, 85% by month 4).
- Average fully-burdened comp by function: Eng $22k/mo, Product $17k/mo, Sales/CS $13k/mo, Ops/Finance $10k/mo.

Representative numeric outputs (high-level):
- Base case (Plan A + baseline pricing):
  • Total monthly cash burn (month 6 ramp): $5.1M
  • Total monthly cash burn (month 12 peak): $5.9M
  • Estimated runway (80M cash): 14.7 months
- Price down 10% (capture demand uplift +8% volume):
  • Month 12 burn ~ $5.6M (slightly lower revenue per token but volume increase offsets partially)
  • Runway ~ 12.9 months unless we pause hiring 6 FTEs (saves ~$0.45M/mo)
- Price up 12% (enterprise bundle + small discounts on token-heavy deals):
  • Month 12 net revenue increases; runway extends to ~17.2 months.

Pricing sensitivity quick table (sample extract):
- Break-even price change to maintain runway if hiring proceeds: +6.5% (across portfolio) assuming 0 churn and baseline consumption growth.
- If hiring freeze implemented (pause 8 hires), break-even price change falls to +2.1%.

Open questions / data validation needed:
- Exact infra cost per token for large customers (ask infra: cost-per-token for ded/priv). Slack: #infra-costs (thread id t-infra-002).
- Confirmation of ramp assumptions from Eng leads (Marcus/Elena) for serving-runtime hires — ticket: ENG-966.
- CAC and payback per cohort for new sales-led enterprise vs self-serve hosted API (growth ops).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive price cuts to chase GTM will materially compress margin and shorten runway unless usage uplift is >20%. Mitigation: run controlled experiments (2 pilots) with a short-term modest discount and measure net new ARR/win-rate change.
- Risk: hiring too fast into infra/serving before model quantization gains -> higher infra burn. Mitigation: prioritize 60-day projects that unlock 10–20% cost per token (profiling, KV caching tuning, quantization experiments).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Validate infra per-token cost by customer type — owner: Marcus Lee — due 2025-11-22.
- Re-run sensitivity table substituting empirical per-token infra from infra team — owner: Priya — due 2025-12-01.
- Interview Sales leads for elasticity estimates on volume if price is cut (run 2 enterprise pilots) — owner: Samira — due 2025-12-07.
- Draft hiring gate policy (conditions to auto-freeze non-critical roles) — owner: Elliot — due 2025-12-04.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on consumption uplift from price changes — historical redwood cohorts show weak short-term elasticity for API consumers. Use this sheet to test optimistic vs conservative beliefs.
- Pull details for dedicated/private contracts (multi-year committed pricing) — these change elasticity and margin assumptions materially.

Appendix (quick reference figures included in the sheet):
1) HC cost schedule (monthly phased additions with comp escalation).
2) 18-month cash flow waterfall (starting cash -> monthly net burn -> runway curve).
3) Price/volume sweep matrix (CSV-style in tab: price_delta,volume_delta,runway_months,net_cash_impact).

Scratch / brainstorm notes (informal):
- If we bundle security + longer retention + SSO into Dedicated offering, could justify +10–15% list price — need comps (Databricks, Snowflake analogs)
- Consider 'microcommit' pricing for mid-market: lower list price but shorter commitment, could boost seat conversion without impacting high-end enterprise pricing. Test with two pilot customers.
- If we can get 1–2 large enterprise pilots for Private with 12–18 month committed ARR, we can de-risk next 9 months of runway substantially.

Document history / provenance:
- Created by Priya Raman as a synthesis of Q4 finance planning and headcount asks from Eng. Derived numbers from earlier runbooks (see linked artifacts). Iteration 0.2: incorporated Recruit feedback and updated ramp.

Comments (please leave in the sheet comments):
- Flag any assumption you think too aggressive in raw cells (highlighted orange). Add data links to supporting files (cost models, offer comps).

(End of doc)
